key_insight: Upstream acoustic forcing drives all three mesoscale flame regimes into a common oscillating FREI (O-FREI) state, where stronger forcing increases forcing-frequency oscillations while reducing mean heat release and the ignition-extinction Strouhal number.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict and manage combustion stability in confined mesoscale devices such as portable power systems and micro-propulsion combustors under acoustic disturbances.
method: Tested three flame regimes: FREI, stable flames (SF), and propagating flames (PF).
Applied upstream acoustic forcing at the combustor tube’s first harmonic over a broad range of pressure intensities.
Used reduced-order mathematical models to complement and interpret the observed flame responses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports regime-dependent observations across a broad range of forcing intensities, showing a transition at higher acoustic pressures to a shared O-FREI behavior.
watch_item: The findings are based on a specific confined mesoscale combustor and first-harmonic forcing, so broader applicability to other geometries or forcing spectra should be validated.
paper_title: Response of Confined Mesoscale Flames to Acoustic Forcing
